name: SANS-CNN sensitivity
source_location: Table 4 (Parameter sheet), row "SANS-CNN sensitivity"
original_study_context: Kamran et al. 2024, npj Microgravity. A convolutional neural network classifying OCT B-scan images for optic disc edema. Performance was measured on image classification, not on a longitudinal SANS-progression outcome.
original_study_endpoint: OCT B-scan image classification (optic disc edema present/absent) - not SANS-progression prediction
permitted_use: Describes OCT B-scan image-classifier performance only. This system is explicitly not an image-analysis model and does not run this classifier; scan results arrive as structured values. May only be considered, in a future phase and with explicit human approval, as the assumed reliability of an externally/offline-produced structured OCT finding. Must never be used as a generic SANS-progression likelihood ratio and must never be used as evidence for venous stasis.
limitations: Document status: "Open paper" - not yet independently checked by this team against the primary Kamran et al. 2024 paper. Single-study figure; no independent replication reported in the source.

permitted_use: Same restriction as sans_cnn_sensitivity: OCT image-classifier performance only, not a validated SANS-progression likelihood ratio, not usable for venous stasis.

permitted_use: Same restriction as sans_cnn_sensitivity: OCT image-classifier performance only, not a validated SANS-progression likelihood ratio.

name: Jugular stagnant or retrograde flow in long-duration ISS crew
source_location: Table 4 (Parameter sheet), row "Jugular stagnant or retrograde flow in long-duration ISS crew"
original_study_context: Marshall-Goebel et al. 2019. Observational ultrasound study of long-duration ISS crew members. Reports a prevalence count, not a diagnostic sensitivity/specificity figure.
original_study_endpoint: Observed jugular flow direction in real ISS crew (descriptive prevalence, not an accuracy or probability study)
permitted_use: Describes observed prevalence of stagnant/retrograde jugular flow in a real ISS cohort. May inform how common venous stasis findings are made in synthetic scenario design. Must not be conflated with, or used to predict, thrombosis - venous stasis and confirmed thrombosis are different findings, and this system does not model thrombosis.
limitations: The source document separately notes "occlusive thrombosis cases reported" in this cohort (Aunon-Chancellor et al. 2020) - that is a related finding from a different paper, not part of this parameter's value, and must not be merged into it.

name: Jugular cross-sectional area by gravity level
source_location: Table 4 (Parameter sheet), row "Jugular cross-sectional area by gravity level"
original_study_context: Lee et al. 2020, Frontiers in Physiology. Parabolic-flight analog study, n=9 subjects, measuring jugular cross-sectional area at discrete simulated gravity levels.
original_study_endpoint: Jugular cross-sectional area vs. simulated gravity level (geometry, not a venous-stasis probability or risk study)
permitted_use: Reference geometry only - expected jugular area at a given gravity level, for synthetic data generation and sanity-checking simulated measurements. Not a risk or disease cutoff: the source gives no threshold area above which venous stasis is indicated, and these values must never be read directly as a venous-stasis probability.
limitations: Small sample (n=9); parabolic-flight analog rather than sustained microgravity or partial-gravity exposure. Moon (0.16g) and Mars (0.38g) are not among the directly tested levels.

name: ONSD abnormal cutoff, adult (for ICP above 20 mmHg)
source_location: Table 4 (Parameter sheet), row "ONSD abnormal cutoff, adult (for ICP above 20 mmHg)"
original_study_context: Derived from ICU / neurocritical-care literature correlating ONSD with invasively-confirmed intracranial pressure (ICP) above 20 mmHg. The measured population is ICU patients with suspected raised ICP - not astronauts, and not SANS.
original_study_endpoint: Intracranial pressure (ICP) diagnosis in ICU/neurocritical-care patients, threshold ICP > 20 mmHg - not SANS progression
permitted_use: ESTABLISHED only as an ICU/ICP diagnostic cutoff. The source document's own label is: "Established for ICU ICP; Assumption when applied to SANS." ICP diagnostic evidence is not validated SANS-progression evidence. Any use of this cutoff to flag SANS progression is an unresolved ASSUMPTION requiring explicit human approval (see assumption registry entry onsd_icu_cutoff_reuse_scope). This entry alone does not authorize that use, and it must never be silently treated as a SANS-progression threshold.
limitations: Different population (ICU patients vs. astronauts) and different endpoint (confirmed raised ICP vs. SANS progression). The source document itself cautions that ONSD is better treated as a semi-quantitative trend marker than a fixed-threshold test (see onsd_baseline_spread_assumption).

name: ONSD accuracy: Koziarz 2019 meta-analysis (cutoff 5.0 mm)
source_name: Koziarz et al., Ann Intern Med 2019
source_location: Table 4 (Parameter sheet), row "ONSD accuracy: Koziarz 2019 meta-analysis (cutoff 5.0 mm)"
original_study_context: Meta-analysis of ONSD ultrasound accuracy for detecting elevated intracranial pressure at a 5.0mm cutoff. Reference endpoint is ICP, not SANS progression.
original_study_endpoint: ONSD vs. invasively/clinically confirmed intracranial pressure (ICP) - not SANS progression
permitted_use: Established as ONSD-vs-elevated-ICP diagnostic accuracy. ICP diagnostic evidence is not validated SANS-progression evidence. The source document proposes this as the base-case likelihood-ratio pair IF a SANS Bayesian probability model is approved in a future phase. Per explicit project direction, this is NOT YET a validated SANS-progression likelihood ratio and must not be used in any probability calculation until that approval occurs.
limitations: ICP reference standard, not SANS progression. Sensitivity and specificity are as reported by the source study; LR+ and LR- are stated in the document as "Computed" (derived from sensitivity/specificity via the standard formula), not directly reported by Koziarz et al. themselves. One of three differing ONSD accuracy estimates in this sheet (see onsd_accuracy_ohle_2015, onsd_accuracy_maissan_2015); the three disagree on LR+ (7.2 vs 13.7 vs 47), underscoring none is a settled figure yet. SUPERSEDED FIGURE AVAILABLE: see onsd_accuracy_koziarz_2019_rev1 for revised sensitivity/specificity/LR figures provided 2026-11-04 - this original entry is preserved unchanged for traceability, not replaced.

name: HRV change per mm of ONSD
source_name: HDT physiology studies; Helissen 2022 (mouse, -30 degree hindlimb unloading, days S1 to S5)
source_location: Table 4 (Parameter sheet), row "HRV change per mm of ONSD"
original_study_context: Head-down-tilt physiology and a mouse hindlimb-unloading (-30 degree tilt) model. Reports a direction of autonomic change that flips over time - vagal surge in the first 24h (heart rate down, RMSSD/SDNN/HF up, baroreflex gain up), sympathetic shift after about 72h (heart rate back to baseline, blood pressure up, LF up, so HF falls and LF/HF rises only in this later phase) - not a coefficient linking HRV to ONSD. The document is explicit that no coefficient in a usable unit (e.g. ms of RMSSD per mm of ONSD) exists anywhere in the sources.
original_study_endpoint: Autonomic (HRV) response time course in a mouse hindlimb-unloading model - animal, not human, and not a validated human predictive coefficient
permitted_use: The document states explicitly that no coefficient exists relating HRV to ONSD change (no ms of RMSSD per mm of ONSD). Mouse physiological observations are not validated human astronaut predictive coefficients. If used as an adaptive-trigger signal in a future phase, the assumed predictive accuracy must be swept as an explicit, labeled assumption (see assumption registry entry hrv_trigger_assumed_accuracy) across multiple simulation runs - never asserted as a known, fixed, validated accuracy. Any simulated HRV drift must be time-dependent (sign changes between the <24h and >72h phases), not a fixed sign.
limitations: Primarily mouse data, not human; not shown with daily wearable data in orbit; the reported direction is phase-dependent, not a single coefficient.
